captions.instagram:
Heat a gas from 0 °C to 273 °C at the same pressure. Its volume becomes? A ×1.5 · B ×2 · C ×273
Comment your guess before you watch 👇

Class 11 Chemistry · States of Matter (Gas Laws)
Chemistry, visualised #4

The molecules speed up and push the lid higher: the volume doubles → B.
Why ×2? Draw volume against temperature and extend the line backwards: it hits zero volume at −273 °C, absolute zero. Measured from there, 0 °C is 273 K and 273 °C is 546 K. Double the kelvin, double the volume. That's Charles's law: V ∝ T (in kelvin).
